tasks.short: Collect time sheets, type hours, check them against the roster, approve and pass them to payroll, track hours against budget and record sick reports.

steps.what: Cleaners record start and end times: on paper sheets today, by clocking in and out with the site tag after the change
Supervisor collects paper time sheets from cleaners
Supervisor types work hours into the hours spreadsheet
Supervisor checks hours against the roster and corrects errors
Supervisor checks and approves the period's hours per cleaner against the roster and known absences
Supervisor releases the approved hours to payroll: by e-mail today, by one release in the planning system after the change
Supervisor tracks hours against the site budget in a spreadsheet
Supervisor records sick reports and expected return dates

tasks.design: Cleaners clock in and out with a QR or NFC tag at the site entrance in the planning system's app ({HCM}); no location tracking is used. Hours land in the system, which lists only deviations from the roster for the supervisor to correct. After the supervisor approves the period, hours flow to {PAYROLL}, and a dashboard shows hours against each site's budget. The supervisor records sick reports as today, with dates only, never the cause.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper time sheets were typed into spreadsheets and mailed to payroll.
tasks.enabler_now: Cleaning operations suites offer clock-in by QR or NFC linked to payroll.
tasks.still_hard: Forgotten clock-ins still need fixing; clock data can be used to watch staff.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that a cleaner stayed late to help a colleague and making sure it is paid.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor approves deviations instead of typing hours.

evidence.claim: FacilityApps offers clock-in by GPS, QR or NFC linked to payroll.
The data protection authority fined a maintenance company EUR 15,000 for recording sickness causes and leaving absence records online without authentication.
Clock-in tied to named cleaners can check attendance, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from hours worked to payroll and budget view; pay calculation is outside.

Input contract for s1 and s2: start and end times clocked by cleaners with the site tag in the planning system's app (s8), replacing the paper sheet; published roster from the planning system; site budgets set by the operations manager; fallback is paper time sheets.
Checking and approving hours keep their full time; s5 keeps 10 for the release itself. s6 keeps 40 because reading the budget view and acting on it stay. s7 is a first record and keeps its full time.
Payroll staff time is outside the supervisor's savings.
Coverage: about 85% of shifts are clocked; for the rest the supervisor still collects paper sheets (s1 keeps 15) and types them in (s2 keeps 15), and fixes forgotten clock-ins.
unknowns: Whether the works council agrees to clock-in.
research_questions: Do payroll corrections fall after clock-in?

approvals.approved_version: The period's hours per cleaner and site exactly as checked by the supervisor in s4, released once to {PAYROLL} for this pay period; any later correction needs a new check and release.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of shifts are clocked because smaller sites keep paper sheets (47.5); high: 85% of shifts clocked as assumed (63.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Get isolation notices, assign trained cleaners, instruct on protocol and protection, check the cleans, record them and report problems.

steps.what: Supervisor receives isolation notices from wards: by phone today, as a task in the cleaning app after the change
Supervisor assigns trained cleaners to isolation rooms
Supervisor directs cleaners on the protocol for stopping the spread of infections
Supervisor checks that isolation cleaning was done properly
Supervisor records completed isolation cleans on paper
Supervisor reports problems to the infection prevention team

tasks.design: When a ward sets or lifts isolation in the electronic health record ({OTHER}), the cleaning task app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) gets a task with only the room and isolation type, never the diagnosis, so no phone call is needed. The supervisor records the check of each isolation clean in the app instead of on paper; this first record keeps its time. Assigning, instructing, checking and reporting stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Isolation notices came by phone and cleans were logged on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Hospital records can pass room-level status to task apps.
tasks.still_hard: Late notices still come by phone; protocols must be followed step by step in the room, not in the app.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a cleaner take off gloves in the wrong order and stopping them.

reach.learn: Whether tapped records make audits faster.

evidence.claim: Hospital records can pass room-level isolation status to cleaning task apps.
Isolation status reveals health data; share only room and isolation type.

assumptions: Boundary: from the isolation notice to reported problems; infection policy is outside.
Input contract: isolation status set by ward nurses in the record; protocols set by the infection prevention team; fallback is phone and paper.

Assigning, instructing, checking, recording and reporting keep their full time; s1 keeps 20 for reading each task in the app. The nurse setting isolation in the record is the release of the notice; the interface sends only room and isolation type.
Records are about rooms, not used to rate cleaners.
Input contract for s1: isolation status set by ward nurses in the record as they do today; the record-to-cleaning-app interface is run by hospital IT; late or missed flags still come by phone.
research_questions: Is the time from notice to isolation clean shorter?

incremental.description: Supervisor handles late notices still phoned in.
Hospital IT keeps the record-to-cleaning-app interface running.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: wards set about half of isolations late, so those still come by phone (5.0); high: most notices arrive as app tasks (11.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Spot wear on rounds, request repairs with photos, get quotes, recommend options, schedule work around occupancy and check it.

steps.what: Supervisor notes wear and damage to furnishings and equipment on rounds
Supervisor writes requests for painting, repair work and replacement
Supervisor checks the final request: room, work needed, photos and urgency
Supervisor submits the checked request to the facility team
Supervisor gets quotes from contractors by phone and e-mail
Supervisor recommends options to the facility manager
Supervisor schedules contractor work around room occupancy
Supervisor checks the finished work

tasks.design: Requests for repair, painting or replacement go into a form with photos in the facility system ({OPS_SYSTEM}); the supervisor still writes and checks each request and submits it once. The scheduling screen shows room occupancy so work can be booked into empty periods. Spotting wear, getting quotes, recommending and checking work stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were written on paper and occupancy checked separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Facility systems hold request forms with photos and show occupancy.
tasks.still_hard: Contractors' availability rarely matches empty rooms.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a stained carpet can last another season.

reach.learn: Whether photo requests make budget choices easier.

evidence.claim: FacilityApps offers digital work orders and dashboards for cleaning companies.

assumptions: Boundary: from wear found to work accepted; purchasing decisions are outside.
Input contract: occupancy from the hotel's property system; request form set by the facility manager; fallback is paper.
Spotting, writing and checking requests, quoting, recommending and checking work keep their full time; s5 keeps 70 because occupancy is on the same screen instead of looked up separately.
Facility manager time is outside the supervisor's savings.

approvals.approved_version: The request with room, work needed, photos and urgency exactly as checked by the supervisor in s2b, submitted once to the facility team's queue in the facility system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: occupancy is not linked to the facility system, so only the request form changes and photo time is a cost (-0.5); high: occupancy shown on the scheduling screen (4.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend the daily briefing, get changes from other departments, adjust cleaning plans, report finished requests and resolve conflicts.

steps.what: Supervisor attends the daily briefing with front office, maintenance and events
Supervisor phones other departments about late checkouts, events and arrivals
Supervisor coordinates cleaning plans with other departments so services are provided on time
Housekeeper marks the special request done on the housekeeping board
Supervisor tells departments when special requests are done: by e-mail today; after the change the done mark shows on their board and the supervisor follows up only exceptions
Supervisor resolves conflicts between departments

tasks.design: Late checkouts, room moves, event set-ups and special requests entered by other departments in the hotel's property system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) appear on the housekeeping board, so fewer calls are needed to find out what changed. When housekeepers mark a special request done, the requesting department is told automatically. The briefing, adjusting plans and resolving conflicts stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes travelled by phone and done requests by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Hotel property systems share changes and request status across departments.
tasks.still_hard: Not every change is entered; some still arrive by phone.
tasks.human_edge: Getting events and housekeeping to agree on who moves the tables.

reach.learn: Whether shared request status cuts follow-up calls.

evidence.claim: Hotel property systems share changes and request status across departments.

assumptions: Boundary: from the briefing to resolved conflicts; guest complaints are outside.
Input contract: changes entered by front office, events and maintenance staff in the property system; fallback is phone.
The briefing, adjusting and resolving do not change.

Other departments' time entering changes and the housekeeper's done mark (s6, share 1, replacing a radio call) are outside the supervisor's savings. The done mark is an ordinary save on the shared board, so it needs no approval.

incremental.description: Supervisor checks the board for changes during the day.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: other departments enter only half of their changes, so calls drop by a quarter (12.5); high: most changes are on the board (18.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The housekeeping supervisor keeps infection control, people and judgement; time sheets, calls and paper logs shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor whose records are done by the end of the shift without a spreadsheet.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Housekeeping and Janitorial Workers
